A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same GRAPHIC paper, including complete main text and Appendices A.1–A.16. The text, equations, tables and rendered figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR-100 and Tiny ImageNet experiments, graph analyses, robustness studies and a 31-participant image-labeling study.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and human-study results, with revised assortativity results in Figures 3, 44 and 45.

M1.justification: The graph-analysis component changes its assortativity calculation in Equation (2). The linear classifiers, mixed-label loss, confusion-matrix construction, graph generation and modularity-based community detection remain unchanged.

E1.justification: CIFAR-100, Tiny ImageNet, the human-labeling study and the existing modified-image and random-group scenarios are retained. No dataset, task or population is added or removed.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparison sets remain unchanged, including the ResNet-50 reference accuracy curves in Figures 11–12 and regularized versus unregularized classifiers in Figures 15–18.

E3.justification: Equation (2) revises the assortativity metric used in the existing evaluations, with corresponding plot updates. The stated splits, training budgets, model configurations and grouping protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.13 revises the existing analysis of group-size effects and random assignments using the corrected assortativity calculation. Figures 44–45 update the evidence for these controls; no new ablation or robustness experiment is introduced.

E5.justification: Repeated-run and uncertainty reporting are unchanged. Appendix A.6 and Figure 21 retain the five-seed modularity analysis with means and three standard deviations.

E6.justification: Figures 3 and 44 show lower assortativity values under the revised definition. In Figure 45, the random two-group values described as around 0.3 in v1 become slightly negative in v2, while other random groupings remain near zero. These are revised-metric results, with the other empirical findings retained.

T1.justification: Equation (2) replaces the squared Frobenius norm, ||E||_F^2, with 1^T E E 1 in both numerator and denominator. This changes the mathematical definition and its chance-mixing correction; it is not equivalent notation. Other definitions and equations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about architecture-agnostic class-level analysis, identifying dataset issues and studying linear separability.

C2.justification: Appendix A.13 withdraws the explanation that random two-group assignments produce weak group structure by grouping similar categories together. It now interprets the results as showing no genuine structure, with a small disassortative tendency substantially weaker than the effect of meaningful semantic grouping.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, hardware, runtime measurements, practical guidance and code-access information remain unchanged, including Section 5.1 and Appendices A.7–A.8.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography and research positioning in Section 2 and Appendix A.1 are unchanged, including the comparison with Confusion Graph.

P1.justification: One paragraph in Appendix A.13 is rewritten to explain the revised random-group findings, and the notation explanation following Equation (2) changes. The document's broader wording and organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 45 receives a tighter vertical scale that includes negative assortativity values. Figure numbering, captions, table structures and overall page organization remain essentially unchanged.

improvement.justification: The corrected Equation (2), updated plots and revised Appendix A.13 remove the misleading interpretation of positive assortativity under random grouping, improving this analysis's validity. The improvement is localized and incompletely integrated: Section 5.2 still calls first-epoch assortativity 'fairly high,' although revised Figure 3 starts below the paper's stated moderate-assortativity threshold.
